Scripture links them with the Anakim and the Zamzummim (Deut 2:11, 20), painting a picture of formidable peoples displaced by divine mandate. German 'Totengeister' intriguingly echoes the homonymous connection to shades of the dead, though here the term is purely ethnic."

They appear in the Table of Nations context (Gen 15:20), in Og's kingdom of Bashan (Deut 3:11; Josh 12:4), and in the Valley of Rephaim near Jerusalem (2 Sam 5:18, 22). The name is distinct from the homonymous 'shades/dead' usage of the same root.
    Existing Spanish translations: Refaim, Refaím, los-refaim, los-refaitas, los-refaítas, refaim, refaitas, y-el-refaíta
